new_statements.rule_in_words: The section headed 'Syllabic structure and stress' gives no placement rule: it only says the central vowel ɨ occurs exclusively in unstressed syllables, that vowel length may be conditioned by stress, and that word boundaries are re-syllabified in noun and verb phrases. Acute accents in the paper's transcriptions fall on mixed positions: penult in Hénnet, béHin, sá¿a, walédda, bisídda, taná¸¸ef, tana¸éff-o (stress moves right when a suffix is added), betúm-mÂ, beHát-tu; final in dahÂlík, ¿abbáy, nahár; these are the author's markings, not a stated rule, and are not enough to assign a type.
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; the author flags the vowel system as 'remains to be set up'
new_statements.identity_note: Simeone-Senelle's data are from Dahlak Kebir (also Nora, Dehil and Massawa speakers) and describe the language the speakers call dahālík; she classes it as a separate Afro-Semitic language close to Tigre, while Kapeliuk's review (Aethiopica 14, 2011) records the competing view that it is a Tigre dialect. Both listed 2010 works take the 'separate language' side.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated locator in the open-text HAL file we hold, and the cross-check locator in the second held HAL file also verified. The deciding source is the primary (and effectively only) field description of Dahalik, by its sole describer; it presupposes stress but states no placement, weight or lexical-contrast rule and says the vowel phonology 'remains to be set up', so not determinable/not stated by the source is the honest coding. Glottolog's whole descriptive bibliography is three items by the same author; web and HAL searches turned up no phonology paper, instrumental study, dissertation or grammar. The only unheld item of note is the 2010 19-pp. sketch (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description), print/login-walled, which a contemporary review characterises as verbal-system-focused; obtaining it is worth a medium-priority library request but is unlikely to change the classification.
